Here is the reasoning: PC culture is an extreme response to aspects of our culture that some people think should be shunned. PC culture uses a totally inappropriate and some might call "stupid" response to most any and all reasonable people and should NOT be used by people on a day to day basis. Now, the ideals behind PC culture arguably do make some sense when applied to extreme vulgarity and extremely bad things. I feel like an example is useful at this point to clarify:

* Jack wearing a nazi uniform to work and screaming obscene things about jews - Shunned. * Jack going to work wearing a Trump t-shirt and talking to people about Trump - Not shunned. * Jack running around beating up gay people - Shunned. * Jack telling people he doesn't agree with the gay lifestyle - Not shunned.

You can argue these points if you want, but for the moment lets assume these value judgements are sound when it comes to things that should and shouldn't be shunned. Now, lets focus on Voat, and the very strong Anti-PC culture we have going on here. The response I see most here on Voat is not "PC culture is extreme, be more reasonable", but rather "PC culture is extreme, you should be firmly against all PC culture ideals!". The end result is that rather than countering PC culture with a reasonable stance that everyone can get behind, the extreme opposite of PC culture has taken root, and it results in people being pushed out of the conversation because there is no in-between. When very clearly, any reasonable rational person understands that there is a lot of room in the middle here that most of us can agree on.

The conclusion is this: If you want to oppose PC culture because of it's extreme ideals, reject the extremes in all forms, push people towards a rational and reasonable goal, not a goal of rejecting everything just because you disagree with some parts of it. Pushing people to reject everything pushes people towards another extreme, which, in the end would be just as bad as PC culture.
